# Goal

Take a neuron from the
[hemibrain connectome](https://www.janelia.org/project-team/flyem/hemibrain),
use [NeuronBridge](https://neuronbridge.janelia.org/) to find GAL4 and
LexA lines that label it, and combine two of those into a
[split-GAL4](https://www.janelia.org/lab/rubin-lab/our-research/gal4-driver-lines/split-gal4-lines)
that targets just that one cell type. The example here uses **LAL051**,
a local neuron in the LAL that drives descending motor circuits — a
plausible target for sparse genetic access.

## See the EM target in 3D

`hemibrainr` fetches the skeleton split into axon and dendrite:

```{r LAL051, eval = FALSE}
# Load a package we will need
library(hemibrainr) # to get this to work, please see:

# Find out neuron of interest
LAL051.info = neuprint_search("LAL051", field = "type")
LAL051.id = as.character(LAL051.info$bodyid)
LAL051.n = hemibrain_read_neurons(LAL051.id)

# Get the LAL
lal = neuprint_ROI_mesh("LAL(R)")

# Plot this neuron
nat::nopen3d()
plot3d(hemibrain.surf, col = "grey", alpha = 0.1)
plot3d(lal, col = hemibrain_bright_colors["red"], alpha = 0.1, add = TRUE)
hemibrain_view()
plot3d_split(LAL051.n, lwd = 2, soma = 400)
### Dendrite in blue, axon in orange, outouts in red, inputs in navy blue
```

![LALtargetEM](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/natverse/neuronbridger/main/inst/images/LALtargetEM.png)

## Render the target as a colour-depth MIP

NeuronBridge ranks LM lines by **colour-depth MIP** similarity to a
2-D EM render in which hue encodes z-depth
([Otsuna et al. 2018](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/318006v1)).
NeuronBridge already ships pre-computed MIPs for every hemibrain cell:

```{r LAL051.mip, eval = FALSE}
# What do we have on it?
nb.info = neuronbridge_info(LAL051.id)
View(nb.info)

# Let us now see the related MIP file
LAL051.mip = neuronbridge_mip(LAL051.id)
## This gets every MIP file associated with id

# Plot the MIP image in an rgl viewer
clear3d()
plot_mip(LAL051.mip)
```

![LALtarget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/natverse/neuronbridger/main/inst/images/LALtarget.png)

## Search for lines that contain the target neuron

`neuronbridge_search()` returns the LM lines (mostly GAL4) whose MIPs
match the EM query, ranked by colour-depth score:

```{r neuronbridge_search, eval = FALSE}
# Run search, looked at precomputed data
ns.s = neuronbridge_search(LAL051.id, threshold = 2000)

# scan hits
open3d()
scan_mip(mips = ns.s, no.hits = nrow(ns.s))
```

Top hits for LAL051: `R58G03` and `R71D08` — two FlyLight enhancers
that each include the cell, and that the split-GAL4 design step below
combines into a sparser line.

![R58G03](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/natverse/neuronbridger/main/inst/images/R58G03.png)

![R71D08](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/natverse/neuronbridger/main/inst/images/R71D08.png)

## Predict the split

`neuronbridge_predict_split()` intersects the matching neurons in two
hemidrivers and reports the cells likely to survive in their
split-GAL4. Fewer surviving cells = sparser line.

```{r LAL051.design.split, eval = FALSE}
line1 <- "R58G03"
line2 <- "R71D08"
potential.split <- neuronbridge_predict_split(
  line1 = line1, line2 = line2,
  threshold1 = 2000, threshold2 = 2000)
message("Predicted: ~", nrow(potential.split), " neurons in this split")
View(potential.split)
```
